title: Pre-Board 5 Mathematics
subject: Engineering Mathematics
description: 100-question Pre-Board 5 Mathematics reviewer with formulas, solutions, explanations, and an iPad/Apple Pencil solution pad.

questions.solution: For a scalar field, the maximum directional derivative is |∇V|. With V=2xy+z², ∇V=(2y,2x,2z); at (1,1,1), |∇V|=√(4+4+4)=√12 → A. The other choices are not the gradient magnitude.
x=5cosθ and y=5sinθ satisfy x²+y²=25, so the path is a circle → D. A line, parabola, or ellipse does not match the equal-radius sine/cosine parametrization.
An odd periodic waveform has an odd Fourier series, so cosine (even) terms vanish → B. Sine coefficients are generally nonzero for an odd square wave.
Circulation density of a vector field is measured by the curl, ∇×F → A. Gradient applies to scalars, divergence measures net outflow, and the Laplacian is a second-order operator.
lim[x→0] sin(3x)/x = 3·lim sin(3x)/(3x)=3 → A. The limit is finite, so 0, 1, and undefined are incorrect.
L{5e⁻³ᵗu(t)}=5/(s+3) → A. The shift is s+3 because the time exponential is e⁻³ᵗ.
Average value on [0,π] is (1/π)∫₀^π sinx dx = 2/π → C. The other values ignore the interval length or the integral.
Newton-Raphson uses xₙ₊₁=xₙ−f(xₙ)/f′(xₙ); if f′(xₙ)=0 the update is undefined → D. It does not require two bracketing guesses.
dQ/dt=−0.10Q gives Q(t)=Q₀e⁻⁰·¹ᵗ=100e⁻⁰·¹ᵗ → D. The other forms have the wrong sign, initial value, or exponent.
Selecting one whole manufacturer group and testing every item in it is cluster sampling → C. Stratified sampling would sample from every manufacturer group.
∫xe²ˣdx is a product of algebraic and exponential factors, so integration by parts is the standard method → C. Partial fractions and trig substitutions do not fit.
Forward cascade transfer functions multiply: G_eq(s)=G₁(s)G₂(s) → C. Addition is parallel combination; the feedback form needs a loop.
∫dx/(x²+3²)=(1/3)arctan(x/3)+C → A. The coefficient and arctangent argument follow the standard a²+x² form.
Gaussian elimination systematically eliminates subdiagonal entries to form an upper triangular matrix → C. Cramer's rule uses determinants instead.
A first-order ODE necessarily contains a first derivative of the dependent variable → C. It need not have constant coefficients, a second derivative, or multiple independent variables.

Source issue: Newton's Law of Cooling is dT/dt=−k(T−Tₘ) for k>0. The PDF's option II shows +k(T−Tₘ), so none of the printed choices exactly matches the standard law; this card is intentionally not graded.
A right-half-plane zero makes a system non-minimum phase → B. System type is determined by poles at the origin, not by an RHP zero.
Because p=0.06 > α=0.05, fail to reject H₀ → B. There is insufficient evidence at the 5% level to call the batch defective.
Set partial derivatives to zero: 12−4I₁−I₂=0 and 16−I₁−2I₂=0. Solving gives I₁≈1.14 and I₂≈7.43 → B. The Hessian is negative definite, so this is the maximum.
Convolution is commutative, associative, and distributive over addition; it does not depend on a nonlinear operator → A.
Marginal cost in x is ∂C/∂x=8x+2y. At x=3,y=5: 24+10=34 → B.
Distinct real roots of a stable second-order homogeneous ODE produce a sum of decaying exponentials → C. Oscillatory sine terms come from complex roots.
If f′(t)<0 over an interval, the function is decreasing there → B. Concavity depends on the second derivative.
For y=(2/3)x^(3/2), y′=√x. Arc length is ∫₀³√(1+(y′)²)dx=∫₀³√(1+x)dx, expression I → A.
Linear convolution length is M+N−1=4+3−1=6 samples → D.
Vertical rectangles parallel to the y-axis and revolved around the y-axis generate cylindrical shells → D. Washers/disks use slices perpendicular to the axis.
For RL step response, I∞=V/R=5 A and R/L=5 s⁻¹, so i(t)=5(1−e⁻⁵ᵗ) → C.
The integral is ∫₀²∫₀ˣ² dy dx = ∫₀² x²dx = 8/3 → A.
By the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus, F(b)−F(a)=∫ₐᵇ f(x)dx → A.
∫cos(kx)dx=(1/k)sin(kx)+C → D. Differentiating confirms the factor k cancels.
For an exponential lifetime, P(T>t)=e⁻λᵗ. With λ=0.01 and t=100, P=e⁻¹ → B.
Divergence theorem converts ∯D·dS to ∭(∇·D)dV, so the volume integrand is ∇·D → B.
The correlation coefficient r measures both strength and direction of a linear relationship → A. R² measures explained variance but loses the sign.
Standard negative feedback gives T(s)=G(s)/[1+G(s)H(s)] → C.
Final Value Theorem: e(∞)=lim[s→0]sE(s)=lim (3s+2)/(s²+4s+3)=2/3 → B.
A Type II error means failing to reject a false null hypothesis, often phrased as incorrectly accepting the false null → D.
For independent samples, Var(x̄)=σ²/n → A. The standard deviation is σ/√n, not the variance.
j has polar form 1∠90°. Its principal square root is 1∠45° → A.
Newton-Raphson for f(x)=x²−5 from x₀=2: x₁=2−(4−5)/(4)=2.25 → A.
Margin of error E=zσ/√n=2.58(5)/10=1.29 μF → B.
For electrostatics ∇×E=0, and Stokes' theorem gives ∮E·dl=0 → C.
Area between curves with g(x)≥f(x) is ∫ₐᵇ[g(x)−f(x)]dx, expression III → B.
Grouping experimental runs into time shifts to control a nuisance factor such as humidity is blocking → C.
The second time derivative of position is acceleration → B. Velocity is first derivative; jerk is third derivative.
A vector field with zero divergence is solenoidal → D. Irrotational instead means zero curl.
Composite trapezoidal rule with h=1: (1/2)[1+2(4)+2]=5.5 C → D.
∬_R 1 dA equals the geometric area of region R → C.
A rational function with distinct linear factors is first decomposed into partial fractions before inverse Laplace transformation → A.
dy/y=2x dx gives ln|y|=x²+C, hence y=Ceˣ², expression I → A.
The complementary/homogeneous solution is the circuit's natural unforced transient response → C. The particular solution gives the forced response.
A steady 2D temperature field with no internal heat source satisfies Laplace's equation ∇²T=0 → C.
A square system Ax=b has a unique solution exactly when det(A)≠0 → A.
∫ acceleration dt gives the net change in velocity → D.
Set x²=2x+3 → x²−2x−3=0=(x−3)(x+1). Points are (3,9) and (−1,1) → B.
Electric field intensity is a vector quantity → C. Magnetic flux, charge density, and electric potential are treated as scalars here.
Two identical real negative roots correspond to critical damping, the fastest nonoscillatory response → A.
f′=3x(x−2), so test x=0,2,3. f(0)=1, f(2)=−3, f(3)=1; absolute minimum is −3 → B.
dy/dx=(dy/dt)/(dx/dt)=4/(4t+1). At t=1, slope=4/5 → A.
Nyquist requires fs≥2fmax=2(20 kHz)=40 kHz → B.
Products LᵢLⱼ in Mason's Δ include only pairs of non-touching loops → C.
Σ(3z)⁻ⁿ is geometric with ratio 1/(3z). Convergence needs |1/(3z)|<1, so |z|>1/3 → B.
For Poisson mean λ=3, P(X=1)=e⁻³3¹/1!=3e⁻³ → D.
A Type-1 system has a finite nonzero steady-state error for a ramp input → A.
Routh first-column signs +,+,−,+,+ contain two sign changes, so there are exactly two right-half-plane poles → A.
Cylindrical azimuth φ=atan2(y,x)=atan(√3/1)=60° → B.
Independent consecutive errors: 0.1×0.1=0.01 → B.
4t²−1=(2t−1)(2t+1). Canceling gives limit 2t+1 at t=0.5, equal to 2 → C.
Real power P=VIcosφ=50·2·cos45°=50√2 W → C.
Ideal white noise has autocorrelation proportional to a discrete impulse at zero lag → A.
By the nth-term test, if lim aₙ is nonzero, Σaₙ must diverge → B. A zero limit is necessary but not sufficient for convergence.
One-dimensional transient diffusion is governed by the heat equation u_t=a²u_xx → C.
x″+9x=0 gives x=Acos3t+Bsin3t. x(0)=4 and x′(0)=0 yield x=4cos3t → A.
m²+4m+4=(m+2)² gives repeated root −2. Thus y=(C₁+C₂t)e⁻²ᵗ, expression II → B.
Main effect A = average at A-high − average at A-low = (20+25)/2 − (10+15)/2 = 10 → C.
Current is the time derivative of charge: i(t)=dq/dt → B.
L⁻¹{4/(s²+16)}=sin4t → C because L{sin at}=a/(s²+a²).
A rectangular frequency-domain spectrum transforms to a sinc-shaped time-domain signal → C.
Differentiate x²y−2x+y²=2: 2xy+x²y′−2+2yy′=0. At (1,1), 2+3y′−2=0, so y′=0 → A.
Vertical velocity is dy/dt=30sin30°−9.8t=15−9.8t. Set to zero: t=15/9.8≈1.53 s → C.
Gauss's law for magnetism states ∯B·dS=0 for every closed surface → A.
V=3x²y²+2x, so ∂V/∂y=6x²y. At (1,2), the value is 12 V/m → A.
Euler: y₁=y₀+h f(t₀,y₀)=5+0.2(−5)=4.0 → D.
A left-half-plane zero attracts root-locus branches toward it, generally pulling the locus left and improving transient speed/stability → A.
For H(z)=z/(z−2), an anti-causal left-sided sequence has ROC inside the pole: |z|<2 → A.
Ampère-Maxwell law: ∇×H = J + ∂D/∂t, i.e. conduction plus displacement current density → A.
For a right-skewed distribution, the long right tail pulls the mean above the median → C.
Critical damping occurs when α²−ω₀²=0, so α=ω₀ → B.
The integral is improper because its upper limit tends to +∞ → B.
KVL for a series RC circuit gives R(dq/dt)+q/C=V(t), expression I → A.
Discrete-time Final Value Theorem is lim[z→1](1−z⁻¹)X(z), expression I. In the listed order, that is choice D.
There are N=3×8=24 observations. Total ANOVA degrees of freedom is N−1=23 → D.
